title: Promotion
description: development → pilot → production — promotion changes which environment runs the code, never the code itself, and every hop adds a human gate.
---

One codebase, three GitHub environments. **Promotion changes *which environment
runs the code*, never the code itself.** Each hop adds a human gate and
increases blast radius.

This page is the condensed operating summary. The concept behind the ladder —
what an [environment](/docs/glossary#environment) is and why promotion never
touches code — is covered in [Environments](/docs/concepts/environments).
Environment gating details, reviewer setup, and rollback procedure live in
[`plugins/gtm-sandbox/skills/gtm-sandbox/references/promotion.md`](https://github.com/nika-loki/paydirt/blob/main/plugins/gtm-sandbox/skills/gtm-sandbox/references/promotion.md)
in the repo.

## Environment configuration (one-time, per repo)

For each of `development`, `pilot`, `production` (Repo → Settings →
Environments):

| Environment | Required reviewers | Deployment branches / tags | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| development | none | all branches | Free-for-all; scratch credentials |
| pilot | 1+ trusted operator(s) | `main` only | First hop with real credentials |
| production | 2+ (or on-call rotation) | `main` or `v*` tags | Real audience; dry-run off |

## The workflow contract

The template (`assets/workflows/gtm-workflow.yml` in the skill) expects exactly:

- A `workflow_dispatch` input `environment` (choice: development / pilot /
  production) and a boolean `dry_run` override.
- The job declares `environment: ${{ inputs.environment || 'development' }}`, so
  GitHub injects the right secrets and enforces that environment's reviewers.
- The app receives `GTM_ENVIRONMENT` and treats any `DRY_RUN` other than the
  literal `false` as a dry run. When the dispatch input is empty (scheduled
  runs), the app derives the default per environment: **dry for development and
  pilot, live for production**.

## Promote

1. Verify behavior in `development` — scheduled or dispatched, failures are
   cheap there.
2. Dispatch with `environment: pilot` → a required reviewer approves → dry-run
   against real credentials.
3. Dispatch with `environment: production` (and `dry_run: false` only if the
   default needs overriding) → two reviewers approve → live.

```bash
gh workflow run gtm-workflow.yml -f environment=pilot -f dry_run=true
gh run watch
```

## Rollback

- **Immediate**: re-dispatch the previous environment configuration
  (`environment: pilot`) — no code rollback needed, because production runs the
  same commit.
- **Credential rollback**: restore the old value in `.env.production` locally,
  re-sync, re-dispatch.
- **Emergency stop**: `gh workflow disable gtm-workflow.yml`, rotate affected
  credentials from the vendor dashboard, then re-sync.

## Anti-patterns

- **Branch-per-environment** (`dev`/`pilot`/`main`) — environments drift into
  different *code*; see [Environments](/docs/concepts/environments) for why
  this fails.
- **Copying `.env.pilot` values into `.env.production`** "temporarily" —
  production gets production-scoped credentials or nothing.
- **Bypassing reviewers for a "quick" production run** — that is what pilot is
  for.
